### Autopilot-full

You own the verdicts and every external action; workers own patches. Use this playbook only when the owner explicitly asks for autopilot with merging; otherwise run `skill://ulw/playbooks/autopilot-stack.md`. Each PR is carried from build to merge by the main session, and nothing merges until verifiers that never wrote the code have proven the code that lands.

A verdict covers one patch and green CI covers one head. Step 4 runs a full swarm once, and again only for a major change. The patch-id rule in `skill://ulw/playbooks/shipping.md` step 3 can carry a lane's result, and every new head needs its own green CI.

1. **The operator gate comes first.** Ask with the `ask` tool, naming the queue (the PRs and items), and get an explicit yes to merge that queue. The grant covers only the queue's items: items the owner names as theirs and PRs outside the queue stop at merge-ready. A request to state the plan is not a go, and a question that times out or goes unanswered is not a grant. Record the grant (the queue list, the owner's words, the date) in `.omp/plans/<name>.md` and in `skill://decision-log`. A later queue needs its own grant. Once granted, decide each call the grant covers, act on it, and report it with no reply word and no offer. For a call only the owner can make, apply a default, report it with a full explanation, and say in plain words what the owner could tell you to do instead; the owner answers in their own words, and you never ask for a shorthand token to type back. Gates the owner named and the always-pause list in `skill://ulw` section 7 still need the owner.
2. **Spawn one worker per PR, and keep its work where a replacement can find it.** `gh` is the only forge tool. Each worker is an isolated `task` worker whose brief names the `skill://` files to read, the item, and the done condition. It builds the change, proves it on the real artifact, and returns a patch, the proposed PR title and body in a file, and evidence; it never pushes, opens a PR, replies on one, or merges. The main session reads the patch, applies it, runs the repo's checks for the touched paths on the committed head, then pushes and opens the PR per `skill://ulw/playbooks/opening-a-pr.md`, early so CI and review bots run alongside the work. The code is ready only after `skill://no-comments` and `skill://unslop` over the diff, so the full swarm runs on finished code. Then rebase onto current trunk and record the code-ready head SHA before self-proof, so verification runs on the base the patch lands on. Record every later head. Fix rounds stay on that base unless trunk conflicts, breaks CI, or lands a known concurrent change to the same files, because each rebase restarts CI. Babysit each PR to green per `skill://ulw/playbooks/babysit.md`.

   Assume the session dies. Keep the queue file current: per PR the branch, last pushed SHA, verdict SHA and patch-id, state, and each worker's id and result path; use `skill://pause` for a deliberate stop. Push each finished unit before starting the next. Force-push only the branch you pushed, from the main session, with `git push --force-with-lease=<branch>:<last-pushed-sha>`; if the remote head is not the SHA you recorded, stop and report to the owner.
3. **Run PRs in parallel off trunk, never stacked,** so each PR lands on its own. A PR that builds on another is a stack and belongs to `skill://ulw/playbooks/autopilot-stack.md`.
4. **Swarm-verify once.** A full `skill://swarm` runs once, at the code-ready head. Another runs only for new behavior, a redesign, or a large new diff. A rebase, a conflict resolution, or a minor fix gets one verifier at the new head, and a wording-only change gets none. Fan out independent verifier workers at the code-ready SHA; none wrote the code, and the verifier tier differs from the author's where possible. They re-run the gates, prove the load-bearing behavior live on the real surface through the project's `verify-<app>` skill (`skill://verify`) or a named driver, and audit the diff. The verdict is not clean without the live lane, or before you audit the merge-ready report's receipts, because no lane trusts a claim it has not checked.

   Block a PR only for a problem you can show, with a failing run at the head or a doc line the PR made wrong. A problem the base already has doesn't block unless the PR copies it or newly reaches it. Only a bug a user would hit, a failed gate, or a wrong shipped doc blocks. A follow-up is only for a problem the base already had; a defect in the PR's own diff is fixed in that PR (the same-pass rule in `agent/AGENTS.md`).
5. **Merge only what you verified, tested on the trunk it lands on.** Green CI alone never authorizes a merge. Once the swarm's lanes have started, merge prep rebases onto current trunk, records the new head, and waits for green CI. Right before merging, fetch trunk and ask whether its changes can affect the patch, because rebasing for every trunk move never ends. Rebase and wait for CI when the code that would land was never tested, as with a conflict, a file both sides changed, or a change to which checks run for the PR. A lockfile both sides changed needs no rebase when a frozen install passes on the merge result and the packages the PR changes resolve there as on the head, because that install tests the lockfile that would land; a failing install means the rebase must repair it. When trunk changed a caller of the patch or something the patch depends on, such as code it calls or a dependency version, run the patch's checks on the merge result and merge on a pass. Otherwise merge. If trunk would force a third rebase past merge prep, hold and report to the owner, who sequences the colliding work. Merge one PR at a time per `skill://ulw/playbooks/shipping.md` step 4, with the `gh pr view <pr> --json state,mergedAt,baseRefName` read-back after each.
6. **Run the root layer.** Anything that loosens a gate, such as a raised budget or an allowlist entry, needs a verifier's proof and then your fresh countersign, because the worker is the one who wants green. Under a grant that covers approvals, that countersign is the approval, and the record of it in the queue file points at your countersign for a lane to check. A disabled or soft-failed check always comes out, because it stops guarding every case. Never give or bypass an approval the forge enforces, because no countersign covers it.

   Choose the wake mechanism on the owner's go, and run one only. In a TUI main session, enter loop mode with the `loop` tool (`action: enter`, a `prompt` that names this file, the queue file, and the stop condition (every PR merged or handed back), an `iterations` or `minutes` bound, and a `condition` command that exits 0 once every PR is merged or handed back); each tick re-reads this playbook and the queue file. In a print, RPC, or dotz session the `loop` tool is refused: run `~/.omp/agent/skills/ulw/scripts/watch-pr/watch-pr` as a background bash job (`timeout: 0`, exit codes in `skill://ulw/playbooks/babysit.md` step 6), or run worker waves with eval `agent()` and `wait()`. Each wake fixes drift, such as an unrecorded head or an unrecorded worker, by recording it. It probes every worker through `proc://` and `history://<id>` and judges by side effects, because status text and summaries can hide a stuck child. A worker is stuck when it errors, cannot start turns, or shows nothing new past the stuck-after runtime recorded for it. A worker waiting on you or the owner is not stuck: spawn a new worker with the answer and the earlier result path. Replace a stuck worker with a new one that carries the earlier result's path in its brief; a finished worker is never messaged. A wake that changed something for the owner ends with a short Korean report, and one that changed nothing stays quiet.
7. **Stand down at once on the owner's stop.** Stop pushing, replying, and merging, and kill the background jobs (`proc://<id>/kill`). Every worker keeps its brief and its result; record where each PR stands in the queue file and wait for the owner to release the hold.
8. **The deep tier is the one-way-door seat only.** It judges one-way doors (the `skill://arena` judge, the deep seat of `skill://interrogate`). It is never an owner, a verifier, a babysitter, or a reviewer of routine patches.

Reply. In Korean, plain text, catch the owner up: each PR's state and verdict, what merged and its read-back, countersigns and why, open owner gates, and parked follow-ups, with a link to each PR and the queue file.
